note: Files the classification rule calls PRODUCTION that are really development, and cannot move yet. Every entry names the reason it is stuck, never the work that will clear it: an enforced artifact records debt, not a plan, so it cannot go stale when planning changes. `resolvedFiles` is the number of entries that resolve to a tracked file, and the lint fails when the live count is ABOVE it (new debt parked here) or BELOW it (a file was fixed and the shrink was not committed). Growing this list is a two-line diff — the entry and the count — and review is expected to challenge it. There is no generator: nothing derives this file, because whether a production-path file is really development is a human judgement.

files.layers/agent-execution/harness-registry/: Production, and the module belongs here — but `callLlm` still reads `LLM_CASSETTE_MODE`, an environment variable only the end-to-end cassette lane sets, and names a development entry point in the error it throws. The import direction is already inverted (the cassette installs itself through `setLlmInterceptor`), so no production file imports a development one; what is left is development knowledge inside a production file. It clears when the lane can be detected without production code naming it.
files.layers/core-ui/src/fixtures/knowledge-da: Mock knowledge items in a production path, imported by the shipping `KnowledgeDetail` page as the fallback when the API returns nothing. Moving the file into a `__` folder would turn a production page into an importer of a development file, which the crossing rule forbids outright — so the fixture cannot move until the page stops needing it. The fix is the API, not a relocation.
files.layers/core-ui/src/pages/_dev/ArtifactDe: A development-only preview page sitting in a production path. `_dev` is one underscore, so the folder clause (`__`) does not claim it, and renaming the folder is not a free fix: `router.tsx` would then be a production file importing a development one. It clears when the artifact surfaces it previews land as real routes and this page is deleted.
files.layers/core-ui/src/router.tsx: Production, and correctly so — but it registers the `/_dev/artifacts` route behind `import.meta.env.DEV`, and that registration is the only thing keeping the development-only preview page reachable. Recorded here as well as the page because deleting the route is the act that clears the page. Two specs under `layers/core-ui/__e2e__/` navigate to it, so it cannot be dropped before they have a real surface to drive.
